At the south-western tip stands Le Morne Brabant, the basalt mountain where people who escaped slavery are said to have hidden, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. At the south-western tip, the trade winds wrap around Le Morne Brabant and blow across a wide, shallow lagoon. That makes it one of the best-known kitesurfing spots in the Indian Ocean, and it's at its best in exactly the months when the rest of the west coast is calm.

The south is the least developed coast. Between Souillac and Gris Gris the reef breaks and the Indian Ocean hits the cliffs directly: dramatic to watch, not a place to swim.
The south-east trade winds blow hardest from about June to August, making the east and south breezy while the west and north stay calm. In the hot summer months, the east's breeze is what you want.

The south-east trade winds blow most of the year but are strongest in winter. They hit the east and south coasts head-on, which means choppy water outside the reef, more cloud and showers, and a cool breeze.

The west coast is in the rain shadow of the island and sheltered from the south-east trades, so it's the driest, sunniest and calmest coast from May to October. It also gets every sunset.
